substance.name: Phenibut
substance.subtitle: GABA analogue · limited clinical efficacy evidence and documented dependence risk.
substance.summary: Phenibut is a chiral CNS depressant with GABA-B and α2δ-related preclinical pharmacology. Human efficacy findings are limited; poisoning, dependence and severe withdrawal are documented.
substance.description: Phenibut is a synthetic GABA analogue, distinct from oral GABA, F-phenibut and baclofen. Parent compound, enantiomers, hydrochloride/free-amino-acid preparations and commercial products must not be conflated. A small randomized add-on study and uncontrolled clinical cohorts report indication-specific improvements; these do not establish broad anxiety, sleep or healthy-person enhancement benefits. [Clinical study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29265084/) · [Recent observational study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12347254/).
substance.evidenceNote: Selected studies from a separate Phenibut Deep Research run, reconciled with primary records; independent editorial review remains pending. The 2025 efficacy cohort was uncontrolled and manufacturer funded, with declared commercial interests. Several older papers were abstract-only. An unverified elimination estimate, absent trial comparator or missing disclosure remains unknown; these gaps must not become evidence of safety, independence or no effect.

doses.note: Clinician-prescribed routine practice; uncontrolled exposure is not a personal recommendation.

effects.name: Reported somnolence
effects.description: Somnolence was the most frequently reported adverse event in the older trials summarized by the review; reporting methods and study quality varied.
effects.magnitude: Reported in 1.89% of participants in the review; not a universal incidence estimate.

effects.name: Anxiety during withdrawal
effects.description: Anxiety and insomnia occurred in published withdrawal cases. These adverse experiences do not establish an acute anxiolytic benefit.

outcomes.name: Adjustment-disorder symptom score
outcomes.description: Scores improved within participants; no concurrent comparator establishes a causal drug effect.

outcomes.name: Fatigue in cerebrovascular disease
outcomes.description: The add-on group reported fatigue improvement; the inspected abstract lacks a numeric between-group estimate and blinding details.
outcomes.population: 53 patients with cerebrovascular disease and persistent fatigue
outcomes.exposure: Noophen plus standard therapy; exposure details unavailable in the inspected abstract
outcomes.magnitude: 30–50% reduction reported in approximately three quarters of the treated group.

outcomes.name: Schulte-test performance
outcomes.description: Improved task performance was reported alongside reduced mental fatigue; this is not evidence of general intelligence or healthy-person enhancement.
outcomes.population: Patients with cerebrovascular disease and fatigue
outcomes.magnitude: Numeric between-group estimate not supplied in the inspected abstract.

outcomes.name: Intubation among reported poison-centre cases
outcomes.description: Intubation occurred among selected reported exposures; without an exposed-population denominator or comparator, this does not estimate individual risk.
outcomes.exposure: Reported phenibut exposure; products and coexposures varied

claims.assertion: R-enantiomer-dependent GABA-B pharmacology was demonstrated in preclinical systems.
claims.context: Binding and animal behavioral experiments, not a human efficacy trial.
claims.limitation: Does not establish human clinical effects.

claims.assertion: Phenibut enantiomers bound the α2δ subunit in rat-brain preparations.
claims.limitation: Human target engagement and clinical analgesia remain unestablished here.

mechanisms.title: GABA-B-related pharmacology
mechanisms.description: Binding and antagonist experiments linked R-enantiomer-dependent effects to GABA-B receptors in preclinical systems. Clinical efficacy does not follow from receptor activity alone.

mechanisms.title: α2δ-related pharmacology
mechanisms.description: Phenibut enantiomers bound α2δ in rat-brain preparations; rodent pain models supported this mechanism. These experiments do not establish human analgesic benefit.

cautions.title: CNS and respiratory depression
cautions.description: Selected poison-centre cases included depressed consciousness and respiratory compromise requiring intubation. Case frequency is not population incidence.

cautions.title: Dependence and severe withdrawal
cautions.description: Published withdrawal cases include agitation, hallucinations, delirium and seizures. Case-management reports do not establish a self-treatment protocol.

cautions.title: Product composition and coexposures
cautions.description: The 2026 FDA alert found undeclared ingredients alongside phenibut in a particular product. Its harms cannot all be attributed to phenibut alone.

interactions.name: Other substances
interactions.summary: FDA warns that co-use with other prescribed or illicit substances can contribute to life-threatening complications. This is a general warning, not a quantified pair-specific interaction.
interactions.context: Regulatory safety alert; no controlled interaction magnitude or universal pair classification is supplied.

tags.label: GABA-B receptor
tags.description: A receptor target investigated through ligand binding and receptor-selective antagonist experiments. A compound's activity in an experimental system does not by itself establish human clinical efficacy.

tags.label: α2δ subunit of voltage-dependent calcium channels
tags.description: An auxiliary calcium-channel subunit investigated as a ligand-binding target. Experimental binding and rodent pain responses are distinct from human target engagement or clinical outcomes.

tags.label: Adjustment-disorder symptom severity
tags.description: Symptoms associated with a defined stress-related clinical disorder, measured with an identified instrument such as ADNM-20. Score changes depend on population, comparator and assessment time; uncontrolled change does not establish treatment efficacy.

tags.label: Fatigue severity
tags.description: Fatigue measured with a named instrument such as MFI-20. Physical, mental and motivational domains and their clinical population must remain explicit; a score change is distinct from performance on a cognitive task.

tags.label: Cognitive task performance
tags.description: Performance on a specified cognitive test, retaining the task, measure and study population. A task improvement does not establish general intelligence or enhancement across unrelated tasks.

tags.label: Invasive airway support
tags.description: A documented clinical intervention such as endotracheal intubation. Counts among reported poisoning cases describe those selected records; they do not supply individual exposure risk without an appropriate denominator and comparison.

relationship.label: Phenibut experimental binding targets
relationship.description: Two separately sourced experimental mechanisms. The arrows describe tested molecular relationships and do not infer human efficacy, analgesia or a recommended combination.
